title: Row Rename Surgeon - Rename DataTable Rows and Keep Every Reference
description:
Unreal renames a DataTable or CurveTable row by re-keying the table and doing nothing else. Every FDataTableRowHandle, every FCurveTableRowHandle and every Blueprint row-name pin keeps the old name and from that moment resolves to nothing. The engine's entire response to a row vanishing from under a Blueprint node is to mark that Blueprint dirty and leave the dead name in place. Nothing warns you.

Row Rename Surgeon renames the row and rewrites every reference to it, then re-reads the saved packages from disk to prove no old name survived.

What it finds

Row names live in three places, and it reads all three:

- row handle properties at any depth, including inside arrays, sets, maps and nested structs

- Blueprint pins whose default is a row-handle struct literal

- the RowName pin of any Blueprint node that also points at the same table, which covers Get Data Table Row and every function call taking a table and a row name

The third is the one no first-party tool can show you. The engine indexes row handle properties as searchable names. It does not index Blueprint pin literals at all, so no Reference Viewer and no asset registry query can tell you a Blueprint has that row name typed into a pin.

Only packages the asset registry lists as referencing the table are loaded. It does not blanket-load your project to read a property.

What it refuses, before it writes anything

- a table that still remembers a CSV or JSON import source, because the next reimport would undo the rename and silently re-break every reference just repaired (the source file is named; pass -AllowImported to accept it)

- a new name that already exists and is not itself being renamed away, because that merges two rows

- a referencing package that will not load, because its references could not be read

- a file it would write that is read-only, or has no file on disk

- a backup that could not be taken

Every refusal ends in "Nothing was changed", and every one is decided before the first byte is written.

What it guarantees

-Apply journals every file it may write, rewrites, compiles each touched Blueprint once, renames the row, saves, then re-reads every saved package FROM DISK and reports any that still names an old row. Exit 0 means that check passed. -Undo=<stamp> restores every backed-up file byte for byte.

CI

-run=RRS -Audit -FailOnBroken exits 5 when any reference in the project names a row that does not exist, so a build job can fail on it. JSON and designed HTML reports both.

Honest about coverage

A row name assembled at runtime, stored in a plain FName outside a row handle, or read from a file the editor never sees, cannot be found by any static scan. The reports say so on every page.

Getting started

1. Copy the RowRenameSurgeon folder into your project's Plugins folder and launch the editor.

2. Survey the project: Tools -> Row Rename Surgeon -> Audit Data Table Row References, or type RRS.Audit in the console. Both are read-only and write an HTML report to Saved/RowRenameSurgeon/Report.html.

3. Preview a rename (read-only): UnrealEditor-Cmd.exe "YourProject.uproject" -run=RRS -Table=/Game/Data/DT_Items -Row=Bronze -To=Copper -unattended -nopause

4. Do it: UnrealEditor-Cmd.exe "YourProject.uproject" -run=RRS -Table=/Game/Data/DT_Items -Row=Bronze -To=Copper -Apply -unattended -nopause

5. Undo it, if you want to: UnrealEditor-Cmd.exe "YourProject.uproject" -run=RRS -Undo=<stamp printed by step 4> -unattended -nopause

6. Fail CI on broken row references: UnrealEditor-Cmd.exe "YourProject.uproject" -run=RRS -Audit -FailOnBroken -unattended -nopause

Run -run=RRS -Help for every switch.
